question: What is the aim of Ayushman Bharat scheme?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Health insurance for the poor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ayushman Bharat** is a flagship health insurance scheme launched by the Government of India under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
 
• The scheme aims to provide **free health insurance coverage of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year** for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
 
• It targets **vulnerable and economically weaker sections** of society, specifically 10.74 crore poor and deprived rural families and identified occupational categories of urban workers.
 
• The program is officially known as the **Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)**.
 
• The scheme is fully financed by the Government of India and is considered the **world's largest government-funded health assurance program.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Benefits:**

 
 
• It covers hospitalization expenses for almost all secondary and tertiary medical conditions.
 
• AB-PMJAY includes pre- and post-hospitalization expenses, diagnostic tests, and medicines.
 
• Over 1,400 procedures are covered under the scheme across public and private empanelled hospitals.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility:**
 
 
• Eligibility is determined based on the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data.
 
• There is no restriction on family size, age, or gender under this scheme.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• The National Health Authority (NHA) is the apex body responsible for implementing the scheme.
 
• Beneficiaries receive an e-card that allows them to access cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• As of 2023, the scheme has positively impacted millions of families by ensuring financial protection against high medical costs.
 
• It is a critical step towards achieving the goal of universal health coverage in India.
